aige: AI governance engineering is the application of engineering practice, systems thinking, product thinking and code, to the governance of AI systems: a capability, not a job title, measured by realised risk reduction and audit-ready evidence.
compliance-legal: AI compliance and legal interpret obligations such as the EU AI Act and GDPR and advise on them; AI governance engineering turns the obligation into an executable control and readable evidence, and needs legal, it does not replace it.
responsible-ai: Responsible AI and AI ethics set the values and principles, fairness, transparency and accountability; AI governance engineering implements those values as running controls, so ethics sets the target and engineering hits it and proves it.
ai-safety: AI safety research studies whether powerful models are safe in principle, alignment and dangerous capabilities; AI governance engineering consumes safety research and engineers the controls and evidence for AI systems in production, it does not conduct it.
grc-engineering: GRC engineering, the parent discipline, applies engineering practice, systems thinking and product thinking to governance, risk and compliance generally; AI governance engineering is its AI specialisation and inherits three of the five stack layers almost unchanged.
mlops: MLOps and LLMOps build, deploy and serve models and pipelines reliably; AI governance engineering governs what MLOps ships, adding policy, evals-as-evidence, registry and assurance as gates on the same pipeline.
ai-security: AI security engineering, the sibling AI governance engineering overlaps with most and often the same person, secures AI systems against attack and delivers a defended system, whereas AI governance engineering delivers a governed and evidenced system.
mrm: Model risk management, in the SR 11-7 banking tradition, validates models at points in time for conceptual soundness and back-tests them; AI governance engineering extends beyond model validation to runtime behaviour, agents, rights impact and continuous evidence.
ai-systems: The object of governance is the AI systems and agents running in production, models, systems, agents, data and the organisation, where an agent that browses, executes code, calls APIs and acts under delegated authority is the object legacy governance can least see.
evidence: Audit-ready evidence is the machine-readable record that the controls fired and the risk fell, produced as a by-product of the build, one of the two tests of the discipline alongside realised risk reduction.
auditors: The second test of the discipline is whether a regulator or auditor can read the proof as machine-readable evidence rather than a reassembled screenshot; continuous assurance is a product an auditor or regulator can query.
